c.tagline: Canal city of classical gardens, Slender West Lake, and refined Huaiyang cuisine.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered (flagfall around 9 CNY) but most locals book via DiDi and pay through Alipay or WeChat; carry some cash, as not all drivers accept foreign cards.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 120 the ambulance service, 119 fire and 122 traffic accidents.

avoid.reason: Watch pockets in holiday crowds along Dongguan Street and at Slender West Lake; otherwise usual city awareness.

hood_desc: The historic walled core in Guangling District, laced with canals and lanes around Dongguan Street, Ge Garden and He Garden — the best base for classical gardens, teahouses and old-town atmosphere.
The scenic quarter wrapping Slender West Lake and Shugang hill, with the Five-Pavilion Bridge, Daming Temple and leafy parkland; postcard Yangzhou and a calm, green place to stay.
The bustling downtown commercial hub around the Wenchang Pavilion, packed with malls, department stores, snack streets and nightlife — central and lively.
The modern western district of wide avenues, business hotels, offices and the railway station; a convenient, contemporary base a little out from the sights.
The regenerated Grand Canal waterfront around Sanwan Park, with riverside walks, museums and quieter modern residential blocks.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; tap water is not potable.

transit.pay: Pay by QR code through Alipay or WeChat, or tap a Yangzhou Tong (扬州通) card; cash is accepted with exact change. Bus fares are around 1-2 CNY and the BRT runs a flat low fare.
transit.hours: Buses and BRT run roughly 6:00 AM to 9:30 PM; DiDi ride-hailing fills the late-night gap.
transit.note: Yangzhou has no metro; a Bus Rapid Transit system on dedicated lanes plus an extensive local bus network cover the city, and the compact old town is easily walked or cycled.

bus: Intercity coaches to Nanjing, Zhenjiang and Taizhou

car.idp: Required (foreign licenses not valid; a temporary Chinese permit is needed)

ferry: Grand Canal and Yangtze River crossings and sightseeing cruises

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to the city center (~50 min)
Taxi to the city center (40-50 min, ~120 CNY)

tip.r: Tipping is not part of the culture and is not expected in restaurants or taxis.

food.name: Yangzhou fried rice
food.desc: The original of the dish copied worldwide: separate grains tossed with shrimp, ham, egg, bamboo and peas, restrained rather than greasy.

places.name: Yangzhou State Guesthouse
places.note: Official standard-bearer for the dish; the kitchen helped write the city recipe.

places.name: Fuchun Teahouse
places.note: Century-old house that serves the fried rice after the morning tea rush.

places.name: Xiyuan Hotel
places.note: Grand old Huaiyang dining room near the lake, popular for banquet versions.

food.name: Wensi tofu
food.desc: A Qing-dynasty knife feat: a block of silken tofu sliced into thousands of hair-thin threads that unfurl in a clear chicken broth.

places.name: Yangzhou State Guesthouse
places.note: Best-known place to watch the knife work done properly; worth ordering ahead.

places.name: Xiyuan Hotel
places.note: Classic Huaiyang kitchen that keeps the dish on the standing menu.

places.name: Gonghechun
places.note: One of the city's three historic tea houses, strong on the old banquet dishes.

food.name: Crab-roe soup dumplings
food.desc: Xiefen tangbao: a translucent skin holding hot crab-roe soup, drunk through a straw before you eat the wrapper. Autumn is peak season.

places.name: Fuchun Teahouse
places.note: Founded 1885 and famous for its steamed buns; queue from about 6.30am.

places.name: Yechun Teahouse
places.area: Fengle Upper Street, by the canal
places.note: Signature crab-roe tangbao and jade-green steamed dumplings.

places.name: Gonghechun
places.note: The third of the old teahouses, known for dumplings and noodles.

food.name: Sanding bun
food.desc: Sanding baozi, a soft steamed bun stuffed with diced chicken, pork and bamboo shoot in a glossy sauce; the emblem of Yangzhou morning tea.

places.name: Fuchun Teahouse
places.note: The house that made the sanding bun famous; order it with the oil cake.

places.name: Yechun Teahouse
places.area: Fengle Upper Street, by the canal
places.note: Does a wuding version with five diced fillings alongside the classic three.

food.name: Dazhu ganxi
food.desc: Pressed tofu cut into fine threads and simmered in rich chicken stock with shrimp and ham; the quiet masterpiece of the tea table.

places.name: Yechun Teahouse
places.area: Fengle Upper Street, by the canal
places.note: Widely rated the benchmark version, served piping hot in a shallow bowl.

places.name: Fuchun Teahouse
places.note: Standard opener before the buns arrive; about 30-50 yuan a head all in.

places.name: Gonghechun
places.note: Old-school room where locals still take the full morning-tea sequence.

food.name: Thousand-layer oil cake
food.desc: Qianceng youga: a steamed sweet cake of dozens of gossamer layers brushed with lard and sugar, cut into diamonds and eaten warm.

places.name: Fuchun Teahouse
places.note: Paired with jade shaomai as the traditional sweet finish to morning tea.

places.name: Yechun Teahouse
places.area: Fengle Upper Street, by the canal
places.note: Also does the red-bean bun if the oil cake has sold out.

places.name: Dongguan Street
places.note: Snack shops along the old street sell it by the piece all day.

food.name: Kuilongzhu tea
food.desc: A house blend of Anhui Kuizhen, Zhejiang Longjing and Yangzhou orchid-scented zhulan, created for morning tea and drunk in a lidded cup.

places.name: Fuchun Teahouse
places.note: Where the blend was invented; refills come free through the meal.

places.name: Yechun Teahouse
places.area: Fengle Upper Street, by the canal
places.note: Serves its own version alongside the dumplings.

food.name: Luyangchun green tea
food.desc: Yangzhou's local green tea from the hills at Yizheng, picked in early spring; grassy and sweet, sold loose all over the old town.

places.name: Dongguan Street
places.note: Row of tea merchants selling the spring pick loose and letting you taste.

places.name: Gonghechun
places.note: Pot of local green tea is the standard accompaniment to breakfast here.

landmarks: Slender West Lake (Shouxihu)
A willow-draped imperial garden lake crossed by the exquisite Five-Pavilion Bridge and White Pagoda—Yangzhou's refined answer to Hangzhou's West Lake.
Ge Garden
A salt merchant's classical garden famed for whispering bamboo groves and four rockery 'seasons' sculpted from differently colored stones.
He Garden (Heyuan)
Hailed as the finest garden of the late Qing, blending Chinese courtyards with Western touches and a 1,500-meter covered walkway.
Daming Temple
A 1,500-year-old hilltop monastery honoring monk Jianzhen, who carried Buddhism to Japan; its Qiling Pagoda surveys Slender West Lake.
Dongguan Street
A Tang-era flagstone street of teahouses, pickle shops and lantern-lit snack stalls running down to the ancient canal gate.
Grand Canal (Yangzhou Section)
Where China's UNESCO-listed Grand Canal began in 486 BC; night cruises glide past illuminated wharves that once made Yangzhou fabulously rich.
Wenchang Pavilion
The round, three-tiered Ming pavilion of flourishing culture stands photogenically marooned on a traffic circle at Yangzhou's very center.
Puhaddin Garden Tomb
The canal-side tomb of a 13th-century Muslim missionary said to descend from the Prophet, evidence of Yangzhou's maritime Silk Road heyday.
Yangzhou Museum & China Block Printing Museum
A twin museum whose treasures include a peerless Yuan-dynasty blue-and-white vase and live demonstrations of ancient woodblock printing.
Wangshi Xiaoyuan (Wang Family Compound)
A meticulously preserved salt-merchant mansion of nearly a hundred rooms, showcasing exquisite woodcarving and the opulent domestic life of Qing Yangzhou.

train.note: China has no international trains from this part of Jiangsu, so all services are domestic. Yangzhou railway station, west of the centre, runs frequent D-series high-speed trains to Nanjing and on towards Hefei, Wuhan and Chongqing; Yangzhou East, opened in 2020, is closer to town and sits on the Lianyungang-Zhenjiang high-speed line. Yangzhou is not on the Beijing-Shanghai high-speed trunk, so for Shanghai you either change at Nanjing or cross the Yangtze to Zhenjiang station. Book on 12306 with your passport, 15 days ahead at most.

bus.note: There are no international coaches. The main Yangzhou Passenger Bus Terminal, southwest of the railway station since 2015, covers Jiangsu and neighbouring provinces, with several daily departures to Shanghai (about 4 hours) including direct runs to Shanghai Pudong Airport; the East Bus Station is a convenient alternative if you are staying near the old town. Nanjing is around 1.5 hours by coach and buses are often quicker door-to-door than the train because Nanjing's stations are far out. Tickets are bought at the terminal counter with a passport.

intl.to: Zhenjiang (China) - vehicle and passenger ferry across the Yangtze from Guazhou, about 15 km south of Yangzhou
intl.op: local Yangtze crossing ferry — tickets at the pier; no online booking

ferry.note: Yangzhou sits on the Grand Canal, but the canal now carries freight barges only and there is no scheduled passenger service on it. The one working boat link is the short Yangtze crossing from Guazhou town to Zhenjiang, a workaday vehicle and passenger ferry roughly 15 km south of the city rather than a tourist route. Sightseeing boats on the Slender West Lake and the city canal loop are excursions within Yangzhou, not transport to it.

half.name: Nanjing
half.blurb: Former imperial capital with Ming-dynasty city walls, the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, and Confucius Temple district.

half.name: Zhenjiang
half.blurb: Yangtze riverside city known for Jinshan Temple built into a hillside and its vinegar-brewing tradition.

half.name: Gaoyou
half.blurb: Ancient canal town with a surviving Ming-dynasty city gate and stretch of the old Grand Canal towpath.
